title: The Armor That Walks
text: A suit of black plate stands in the barrow's mouth, dented by blows that killed whoever wore it last. As you come close it turns its empty helm, slowly, toward the one of you who has killed the least. Then it opens its arms, the way a mother does.

options.label: Let the gentlest of you step into its waiting arms, trusting that it means no harm.

outcomes.text: Plate by plate, the armor closes over them. When the helm shuts, the eyes looking out from it belong to someone else.
It is only armor after all, very old and finely made. It fits them as though it had been forged to their measure.
Its arms close like a trap. Whatever has been waiting inside the plate draws a blade.

options.label: The strongest smashes it apart before it can move again, or tempt anyone else.

outcomes.text: It comes apart like a dropped pot. From the pieces rises a long sigh that sounds almost grateful.
It does not wish to be broken. Whatever moves it has had centuries to learn how to fight.

options.label: Back away and go around it. Whatever wore that armor last did not walk away.

outcomes.text: It watches you leave. That night it stands at the edge of the firelight, its helm turned toward the camp. No one sleeps while it keeps watch.
When you glance back, it is no longer where you left it. The scrape of plate on stone follows you for the rest of the day.
